Class GrantStore

java.lang.Object
iu.oidc.provider.GrantStore
public final class GrantStore extends Object
Hands a grant from one endpoint of this provider to another, behind an opaque reference the client carries.

An authorization code and a refresh token are both references of this kind. The grant is signed with an issuer key and encrypted to a content encryption key generated for that one reference, then written to a data store. The reference handed to the client is that content encryption key.

That arrangement is the point: the store holds a token it cannot read, filed under a digest that cannot be reversed into the key that would read it. Whoever holds the reference can find the entry and decrypt it; reading the store is not enough. The signature is what tells the reading endpoint the grant is one this provider issued, and not one written into the store by something else.

The wrapped token names this provider as both issuer and audience, rather than the client's redirect URI: unlike an access or ID token, a reference of this kind is never shared outside the provider — the client only ever carries the opaque reference, and only take(String, URI, WebKey, String) ever reads what it wraps. There is nothing external for it to be addressed to.

Each kind of reference is filed under a digest of its type as well as its key, so a refresh token cannot be presented where a code is expected: it doesn't merely fail to verify, it doesn't resolve to an entry at all. take(String, URI, WebKey, String) deletes the entry it read, so a reference is good once.

Getting one

The data store arrives through the constructor rather than by injection, so this class has no opinion about how a deployment obtains one and nothing here depends on a container. A deployment binds the store where its container binds resources — typically the same store it keeps authenticated sessions in, rather than a second connection to the same server — and constructs one of these once the store is available, sharing it between the authorization and token endpoints so the two cannot drift apart on how a reference is filed. Nothing here is stateful, since every reference carries its own key, so sharing costs nothing.

  • Method Details

    • put

      public String put(String type, URI issuer, edu.iu.crypt.WebKey issuerKey, Duration ttl, OidcGrant grant)
      Writes a grant and answers the reference that redeems it.
      Parameters:
      type - reference type, either CODE or REFRESH
      issuer - this provider's issuer identifier, named as both issuer and audience since the wrapped token is never read by anything but this provider
      issuerKey - key the grant is signed with
      ttl - how long the reference remains redeemable, which is also how long the entry lives, so a grant that is never redeemed isn't left behind for the store to accumulate
      grant - grant to hand over
      Returns:
      opaque reference

    • take

      public OidcGrant take(String type, URI issuer, edu.iu.crypt.WebKey issuerKey, String reference)
      Reads the grant a reference redeems, and spends the reference.

      The entry is deleted before the token is verified, so a reference is spent by being presented rather than by being accepted. A malformed or unverifiable token cannot be retried against the same entry.

      Parameters:
      type - reference type, either CODE or REFRESH
      issuer - this provider's issuer identifier, which the token must name as both issuer and audience
      issuerKey - key the grant was signed with
      reference - reference presented by the client
      Returns:
      redeemed grant
      Throws:
      edu.iu.IuBadRequestException - if the reference resolves to no entry, or the token it names doesn't verify against this provider's issuer, audience, and expiry
